En 1958, ce philosophe britannique démon: In 1958, this British philosopher takes an argument apart the way a lawyer would: a claim, the data that support it, the warrant linking the two, and the rebuttals. English philosophers shunned the book. American communication professors adopted it, and it is still taught everywhere.
En 1947, il raconte quatre-vingt-dix-neu: In 1947, he tells the same mundane scene ninety-nine times, a long-necked young man jostled on a bus, changing style each time: metaphors, litotes, alexandrines, onomatopoeia. His Exercises in Style are a catalog of figures of speech funnier than any textbook.
Compagne de Périclès, elle tient à Athèn: Pericles' companion, she kept a house in Athens where people came to talk. In Plato's Menexenus, Socrates claims she taught him rhetoric and wrote Pericles' famous funeral oration. Plato may be joking. The comic playwrights, for their part, insulted her without joking.
Le philosophe pessimiste rédige vers 183: Around 1830, the pessimist philosopher writes The Art of Being Right: thirty-eight tricks for winning a debate without being right. The last, when all is lost: get personal, hurtful, rude. He never published it. The text appeared after his death, and has served both sides ever since.
En 1791, elle répond à la Déclaration de: In 1791, she answers the Declaration of the Rights of Man article by article, with a Declaration of the Rights of Woman. Her article X: “Woman has the right to mount the scaffold; she must equally have the right to mount the rostrum.” She was guillotined in 1793 for her writings.
Né esclave dans le Maryland, il apprend: Born enslaved in Maryland, he learns to read in secret, escapes in 1838 and publishes the narrative of his life in 1845. The text is so powerful that some readers doubt a former slave wrote it. To convince them, he gives the real names of his masters, so much so that his friends fear he will be recaptured.
Avocat et consul, il fait échouer la con: Advocate and consul, he foiled Catiline's conspiracy in 63 BC: “How long, O Catiline, will you abuse our patience?” His speeches against Mark Antony, the Philippics, cost him his life. His head and hands were displayed on the Rostra, the platform from which he had spoken.
Policier en Birmanie, blessé à la gorge: A policeman in Burma, shot in the throat in Spain, he saw how words are used to lie. In 1984, the Party creates Newspeak to make certain thoughts impossible to express. His advice from 1946: never use a long word where a short one will do.
